title: Forage Virtual Job Simulations
description: Free, self-paced virtual job simulations built by more than 90 real employers -- including Goldman Sachs, PwC, KPMG, Mastercard, and Johnson & Johnson -- letting students complete realistic entry-level work tasks in software engineering, consulting, banking, data analytics, law, and more. No application, interview, or resume required to start, and simulations can be finished at any pace.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read ('Job simulations are 100% free, open access and self-paced'); no age or country restriction found on the page checked, left null rather than assumed and corroborated by multiple independent secondary sources describing it as open to any age/country

title: The Junior Academy
organization: The New York Academy of Sciences (NYAS)
description: A free, year-round virtual STEM program where teenagers from more than 100 countries work in small international teams, guided by scientist and industry mentors, to tackle real-world STEM Challenges on NYAS's online Launchpad platform. Recruitment runs during spring and winter cycles each year; all programme content and communication is in English.
current_cycle_label: Recruits during spring and winter cycles each year; exact 2026-27 dates not captured on this pass
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read ('The Junior Academy is completely free for participating students... No purchase or payment of any kind is necessary'), which resolved a direct contradiction from a secondary source claiming a $500-750 fee for US students -- the primary page's explicit statement was trusted over the secondary claim

title: Science Mentorship Institute (sci-MI)
description: A free, fully online research-mentorship program pairing high school students worldwide with faculty and graduate-student mentors on original research projects in fields including neuroscience, computer science, and environmental science. Programs typically run 5-7 weeks, starting with small international cohort seminars before moving to one-on-one mentorship, and culminate in an original research paper. The organization states keeping all programs free of charge is a stated priority. One specific sub-program (KEMRI) is Kenya-specific per the same page -- noted, but not treated as limiting the organization's general programs, which are described as open to students from around the world.
current_cycle_label: Multiple programme tracks run through the year; exact 2026-27 dates not captured on this pass
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read ('we provide research training to high school students from around the world at no cost'; 'We make it our priority to make all programs free of charge')

title: Pivotal Essay Contest
description: A free-to-enter global essay competition for pre-university students, with prompts developed in collaboration with Oxford University's Global Priorities Institute and reviewed by an international judging panel. Total prizes of $25,000 are awarded across three placements ($15,000 / $7,000 / $3,000); the top 50 finalists also receive books from the Pivotal Library, and the top 5% are invited to join the Pivotal Circle. Explicitly open worldwide with no nationality restriction stated.
current_cycle_label: Most recent cycle's submission window is shown as closed on the official page as of this research date; next cycle dates not yet announced
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read ('No fees'; open 'Worldwide')

title: The Fountainhead Essay Contest
description: A free-to-enter essay competition for 11th and 12th grade students analyzing Ayn Rand's novel The Fountainhead (800-1,600 words), run in quarterly seasonal entry rounds with different prompts. Prizes range from $1,000 to a $25,000 grand prize. Two independent secondary sources, each quoting what reads as the official contest rules, describe eligibility extending to U.S. citizens, Canadian citizens, and citizens of other countries -- this was not independently confirmed on the Institute's own domain, which returned repeated connection failures during this research pass rather than a content block.
citizenship_restrictions: Two independent secondary sources, each quoting apparent official contest-rules language, state eligibility extends to 'citizens of countries other than the U.S. and Canada' -- not independently confirmed via the Institute's own page, which could not be reached during this pass (repeated connection failures, not a content block)
current_cycle_label: Runs in seasonal entry rounds roughly every three months per secondary-source description; exact current-cycle dates not independently confirmed
verification_status: Corroborated, not directly verified -- the Institute's own domain (aynrand.org) returned connection failures on every attempt this pass; two independent secondary sources (accessscholarships.com, scholarships360.org), each quoting what appears to be the actual contest rules text, agree on the international-eligibility and prize figures reported here

title: The Anthem Essay Contest
description: A free-to-enter essay competition open to middle and high school students (grade 8 through 12, age 13+) analysing Ayn Rand's novella Anthem (600-1,200 words). Multiple independent secondary sources describe it as open worldwide with international students welcome, with a grand prize of $25,000 and additional prizes up to $2,000. The Institute's own domain returned repeated connection failures during this research pass, so this was not independently confirmed against the primary page directly.
citizenship_restrictions: Multiple independent secondary sources describe the contest as open worldwide, with international students explicitly welcome -- not independently confirmed via the Institute's own page, which could not be reached during this pass (repeated connection failures, not a content block)
current_cycle_label: Per secondary-source description, entry deadline is annually May 31; not independently confirmed for the 2026-27 cycle
verification_status: Corroborated, not directly verified -- same access pattern as the sibling Fountainhead contest from the same organization; two or more independent secondary sources converge on worldwide eligibility and matching prize figures

title: Medicine Encompassed
description: A student-led 501(c)(3) nonprofit accepting high school students (grades 9-12) nationally and internationally to contribute to free STEAM/medical educational resources -- as a Writer, Editor, or Resource Creator, or through one of 18 committees supporting the organization's medical curriculum and outreach initiatives. No membership fee stated; applications are accepted on a rolling basis throughout the school year.
current_cycle_label: Ongoing -- rolling admissions throughout the school year
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read ('we accept high school students (grades 9-12) from all backgrounds, both on a national and international scale'); no membership fee mentioned anywhere on the page checked

title: Young Scientists Journal
description: A free, student-run, peer-reviewed, open-access journal publishing original research, reviews, and science-communication pieces by high school and undergraduate students across natural sciences, social sciences, medicine, technology, and the environment. Connects with students from roughly 50 countries; submissions are accepted on a rolling basis via an online form, with initial screening, peer review, revision, and copy-editing stages before publication.
current_cycle_label: Ongoing -- rolling submissions, no fixed window
